consensus_summary: Gehenna (Valley of Hinnom) is the standard NT symbol/term for final post-judgment punishment of the wicked (“hell”), drawing on OT associations with child sacrifice, defilement, and the ‘Valley of Slaughter,’ typically imaged with unquenchable fire; dominant reading is eternal conscious torment, with minority alternatives (annihilation, historical judgment, purgation).
book_summary: A valley-trial carried to a destructive verdict: the Valley of Hinnom (site of counterfeit child-sacrifice, renamed Valley of Slaughter) pictures the judgment that destroys both body and soul; distinct from Sheol.
consensus_core_identification: Valley of Hinnom as the established symbol of final eschatological punitive judgment/hell for the wicked.
book_core_identification: Valley of Hinnom as picture of the judgment that destroys body and soul (distinct from Sheol).
rationale: Minimum cores identify the same referent: the historical Valley of Hinnom functioning as the biblical image of final destructive judgment on the wicked (explicitly via Matt 10:28 language and Jeremiah’s ‘Valley of Slaughter’). Book’s ‘valley-trial…destructive verdict’ phrasing and Sheol distinction are compatible elaborations already present or noted in the consensus; no replacement of the central symbol and no material change in the cases covered.
strongest_objection: Book’s ‘destructive verdict’ wording could be read as quietly favoring annihilation over eternal conscious torment, yet that remains an intra-consensus debate already catalogued and does not alter the shared core identification.
